---
name: mise
description: Runs this repo's mise tasks and edits its mise config — use it before running, adding or changing a task, a tool pin, an env value or an alias.
---

# mise

This repo runs on mise: it pins the tools, holds the env values and runs the
tasks.

## Running tasks

- Run every task as `mise run <task>`; discover them with `mise tasks`. Tasks
  differ per repo, so never assume a task name the table below does not list.
- Work locally under `MISE_ENV=dev`. `setup:all` refuses an unset `MISE_ENV`:
  `MISE_ENV=dev mise run setup:all`.

## Where things live

- `.config/miserc.toml`, `.config/mise.toml` and `.config/mise.<env>.toml`
  hold settings and top-level keys only.
- `.config/mise/conf.d/<section>.toml` holds one section for every
  environment, `.config/mise/conf.d/<section>.<env>.toml` one section for one:
  `[tools]`, `[env]`, `[tasks]` and `[shell_alias]`.
- `.config/mise/tasks/` holds the file-based tasks; `_scripts/` there is the
  library they share.
- `mise.local.toml` is this machine's, gitignored and never committed.
- Lines between `# >>> <name>` and `# <<< <name>` belong to the tool or pack
  that wrote them; edit only the lines outside every block.

## Adding a tool

Write the exact version into the right `conf.d/tools*.toml` file —
`tools.toml` for a tool every environment needs, `tools.<env>.toml` for one —
then run `mise install` — never a bare `mise use`, which writes the
top-level config this layout keeps settings-only.

One pin per tool across all the tools files: a tool two environments need is
pinned once, in `tools.toml`.

## Tasks

<!-- >>> tasks -->
| Task | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `code:all` | Format, lint and security-scan all code |
| `code:count` | Count lines of code |
| `code:format` | Format the repo's files |
| `code:git-config` | Validate the local git-config carries the forge identity and signing setup |
| `code:graph` | Refresh the graphify knowledge graph, run by the graphify-refresh post-commit hook (code only, no LLM) |
| `code:lint` | Lint the repo's files |
| `code:merge:develop` | Land a feature branch on develop — merge it, or open a pull request (MERGE_MODEL_DEVELOP) |
| `code:merge:main` | Land develop on main — merge it, or open a pull request (MERGE_MODEL_MAIN) |
| `code:precommit` | Run the commit hooks over your changed files |
| `code:sec` | Security scan the repo |
| `code:worktrees` | List git worktrees across this repo and every member |
| `setup:all` | Set up everything this repo needs on your machine |
| `setup:mise` | Setup MISE: install the pinned versions, reshim & doctor |
| `setup:worktree` | Initialise a fresh git worktree (lighter than setup:all) |
<!-- <<< tasks -->

# CI builds and the deployed runtime — loaded when MISE_ENV=ci.

# >>> mise
[settings]
# Node only — mise's Node release-key import fails on Linux runners. Uncomment for a Node project:
#   node.gpg_verify = false
# <<< mise

.config/mise.dev.toml.content:
# The developer laptop — loaded when MISE_ENV=dev.

# >>> mise
[settings]
env_shell_expand     = true
status.missing_tools = "always"
# <<< mise

.config/mise.test.toml.content: # Test deltas only, layered on dev (MISE_ENV=dev,test); values go in mise/conf.d/env.test.toml.

.config/mise.toml.content:
# The common base, loaded in every MISE_ENV; mise.local.toml (gitignored, never shipped) holds one machine's overrides.

# >>> mise
# The version `env_conf_d` in miserc.toml was tested on.
min_version = "2026.9.16"

[settings]
activate_aggressive  = true            # let mise shims win on PATH
all_compile          = false           # never build a tool from source
env_shell_expand     = true            # expand $VARS in [env]
gpg_verify           = true            # verify tool signatures (see the CI exception)
lockfile             = false           # do not use a lockfile
pipx.uvx             = true            # every pipx: tool installs through uv
python.compile       = false           # the dev tools' python: a prebuilt binary
python.uv_venv_auto  = "create|source"
raw                  = true            # streams output
status.missing_tools = "always"

minimum_release_age = "10h" # minimum age of a release before it is considered for use

# `mise run` installs nothing before a task body: `setup:mise` owns installs.
task.run_auto_install = false

# Inert while `raw = true`; set so turning `raw` off keeps the log shape.
task.disable_spec_from_run_scripts = true         # prevent run scripts from generating spec files
task.output                        = "interleave"
task.timings                       = true         # enable task timing measurements

# A MARKED POSITION — RUNTIME_BLOCK: one runtime settings line per detected language, below this comment.
node.compile = false
# <<< mise

.config/mise/conf.d/env.dev.toml.content:
# Developer-laptop environment values (MISE_ENV=dev).

[env]
# >>> mise
PRE_COMMIT_HOME = "$HOME/.cache/pre-commit"
# <<< mise

.config/mise/conf.d/env.toml.content:
# Env values every MISE_ENV shares; per-environment ones go in env.<env>.toml. Never a secret.

[env]
# >>> mise
# A MARKED POSITION — REPO_NAME: this repo's folder name, slugified.
# A literal: never derive it at load time, since a linked worktree's folder is named for its branch.
REPO_NAME = "scratch"

# TWO MARKED POSITIONS — MERGE_MODEL_DEVELOP and MERGE_MODEL_MAIN: `direct` merges locally, `pr` opens a pull request.
MERGE_MODEL_DEVELOP = "direct"
MERGE_MODEL_MAIN    = "pr"

# A MARKED POSITION — MEMBERS: member repo paths, space-separated; empty when the members are submodules.
MEMBERS = "api web"

# A MARKED POSITION — PATH_ENTRIES: project-local binary paths, below this comment; empty when none is needed.
_.path = { path = "node_modules/.bin", tools = true }
# <<< mise

.config/mise/conf.d/shell_alias.dev.toml.content:
# Shell aliases — dev only: they need `mise activate`, which CI never runs.

[shell_alias]
# >>> mise
precommit = "mise run code:precommit"
setup     = "mise run setup:all"
worktrees = "mise run code:worktrees"

# A MARKED POSITION — MEMBER_ALIASES: one alias per member repo, named by its slug, below this comment:
#   setup-<slug> = "mise run setup:all --<slug>"
setup-api = "mise run setup:all --api"
setup-web = "mise run setup:all --web"
# <<< mise

.config/mise/conf.d/tasks.toml.content:
# Tasks defined inline; the file-based task library lives in mise/tasks/.

# >>> mise
[tasks.init]
# In the base, not dev: CI needs the task files executable too.
description = "Initialize mise tasks"
hide        = true
run         = "find .config/mise/tasks/ -name '*' -type f -not -path '*/*.env' -exec chmod 755 {} \\;"
# <<< mise

.config/mise/conf.d/tools.toml.content:
# Pins are exact versions, resolved when written; never run a bare "mise use".
# Tools every MISE_ENV needs; a tool one environment alone needs goes in tools.<env>.toml, never in both.

[tools]
# >>> mise
# No runtime here: a language or package-manager pack pins its own.
"npm:@askviraj/linter" = { allow_low_downloads = true, version = "1.1.6" }
# <<< mise

.config/mise/tasks/_scripts/helpers.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash

#MISE description="Helper functions for mise tasks"
#MISE hide=true

# Sourced more than once per run; the guard keeps `readonly` from failing the second time.
if [ -n "${MISE_HELPERS_SOURCED:-}" ]; then
  return 0
fi
MISE_HELPERS_SOURCED=1

# Style
readonly BOLD='\033[1m'
readonly NORMAL='\033[0m'
# Colors
readonly GREEN='\033[0;32m'
readonly YELLOW='\033[0;33m'
readonly RED='\033[0;31m'
# Unused here; kept for a task that wants a fourth colour.
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
readonly BLUE='\033[0;34m'

# Print a full-width separator line built from the given character.
line_sep() {
  local COL
  # `|| COL=''` keeps `set -e` from killing the caller when stdin is not a terminal.
  COL=$(stty size 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $2}') || COL=''
  local line
  printf -v line '%*s' "${COL:-80}" ''
  printf '%s\n' "${line// /$1}"
}

# A major section: a full-width `=` rule, then the title.
print_header() {
  line_sep "="
  echo -e "${GREEN}${BOLD}$1${NORMAL}"
}

# A step inside a section: a full-width `-` rule, then the title.
print_subheader() {
  line_sep "-"
  echo -e "${GREEN}${BOLD}$1${NORMAL}"
}

print_success() { echo -e "${GREEN}${BOLD}$1${NORMAL}"; }
print_ok() { echo -e "${GREEN}${BOLD}OK${NORMAL}"; }
print_wait() { echo -en "${YELLOW}${BOLD}$1${NORMAL}"; }
print_warn() { echo -e "${YELLOW}${BOLD}$1${NORMAL}"; }
print_yellow() { echo -e "${YELLOW}$1${NORMAL}"; }
print_newline() { echo ""; }

# Errors go to stderr, so a caller piping stdout into a report still sees them.
print_error() { echo -e "${RED}${BOLD}$1${NORMAL}" >&2; }

# The repo's members, one repo-relative path per line.
# `$displaypath` is git's own variable, single-quoted so git expands it.
# shellcheck disable=SC2016
members() {
  if [ -f "${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}/.gitmodules" ]; then
    git -C "${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}" submodule --quiet foreach --recursive 'echo $displaypath' 2>/dev/null || true
  else
    # Unquoted on purpose: word splitting turns the MEMBERS string into a list.
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    printf '%s\n' ${MEMBERS:-}
  fi
}

# The shell files in scope, one path per line: the paths given as arguments
# filtered down to shell, or every TRACKED shell file when no argument is given.
shell_files_in_scope() {
  local candidates=()
  if [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; then
    candidates=("$@")
  else
    local tracked
    while IFS= read -r tracked; do
      if [ -n "${tracked}" ]; then
        candidates+=("${tracked}")
      fi
    done < <(git -C "${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}" ls-files 2>/dev/null || true)
  fi

  local candidate
  for candidate in ${candidates[@]+"${candidates[@]}"}; do
    [ -f "${candidate}" ] || continue
    case "${candidate}" in
      *.sh | *.bash)
        printf '%s\n' "${candidate}"
        continue
        ;;
    esac
    if head -n 1 "${candidate}" 2>/dev/null | grep -qE '^#!.*[/ ](ba|da|k|z)?sh( |$)'; then
      printf '%s\n' "${candidate}"
    fi
  done
}

.config/mise/tasks/_scripts/merge.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash

#MISE description="The merge both code:merge:* tasks run"
#MISE hide=true

set -euo pipefail
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}/.config/mise/tasks/_scripts/helpers"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}/.config/mise/tasks/_scripts/checks"

# Run the hooks over the whole tree and fail if any rewrote a file: the repair belongs on the branch.
precommit_safety_net() {
  local config="${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}/.config/pre-commit-config.yaml"

  if [ ! -f "${config}" ]; then
    print_warn "No .config/pre-commit-config.yaml — skipping the hook safety net."
    return 0
  fi
  if ! command -v pre-commit >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    print_warn "pre-commit is not on PATH — skipping the hook safety net."
    print_yellow "Run \`MISE_ENV=dev mise run setup:all\` to install the dev toolchain."
    return 0
  fi

  print_wait "Running the hooks over every file ... "
  local hooks_passed=true
  if ! pre-commit run --config "${config}" --all-files >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    hooks_passed=false
  fi

  # The checks refused a dirty tree, so anything dirty now was written by a hook.
  local dirty
  dirty="$(git status --porcelain)"
  if [ -n "${dirty}" ]; then
    print_error "ERROR"
    print_error "- The hooks rewrote files, so this branch was committed without them:"
    while IFS= read -r line; do
      [ -n "${line}" ] && print_warn "  ${line}"
    done <<<"${dirty}"
    print_error "- Commit the fixes on this branch, then merge again."
    exit 1
  fi

  if [ "${hooks_passed}" = false ]; then
    print_error "ERROR"
    print_error "- A hook failed without changing anything, so it needs a fix by hand."
    print_error "- Run \`mise run code:precommit --all\` to see it."
    exit 1
  fi
  print_ok
}

# The `pr` half of the landing model: publish the branch and let the forge merge it.
open_pull_request() {
  local DESTINATION_BRANCH="$1"
  local SOURCE_BRANCH="$2"

  print_wait "Pushing ${SOURCE_BRANCH} to origin ... "
  if ! git push --follow-tags -u origin "${SOURCE_BRANCH}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    print_error "ERROR"
    print_error "FAILED to push '${SOURCE_BRANCH}' to origin!"
    exit 1
  fi
  print_ok

  # `gh` first when both forge CLIs are installed.
  if command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    print_yellow "Opening a pull request into ${DESTINATION_BRANCH} ..."
    gh pr create --base "${DESTINATION_BRANCH}" --head "${SOURCE_BRANCH}" --fill
  elif command -v glab >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    print_yellow "Opening a merge request into ${DESTINATION_BRANCH} ..."
    glab mr create --target-branch "${DESTINATION_BRANCH}" --source-branch "${SOURCE_BRANCH}" --fill
  else
    # Not a failure: the branch is pushed, and opening the request is a click.
    print_warn "No forge CLI on PATH — the branch is pushed, no request was opened."
    print_yellow "  branch:      ${SOURCE_BRANCH}"
    print_yellow "  destination: ${DESTINATION_BRANCH}"
    print_yellow "Open the pull request on your forge."
  fi

  print_newline
  print_success "Branch pushed — the merge happens on the forge."
}

# merge_to_destination_branch <destination> [<source>]
#
# <source> defaults to the current branch; the checks still read the CURRENT branch.
merge_to_destination_branch() {
  local DESTINATION_BRANCH="$1"
  local CURRENT_BRANCH
  CURRENT_BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
  local SOURCE_BRANCH="${2:-${CURRENT_BRANCH}}"

  # The DESTINATION's model; the legacy MERGE_MODEL stands in for an unset one, and anything but `pr` is `direct`.
  local MERGE_MODE=""
  case "${DESTINATION_BRANCH}" in
    develop) MERGE_MODE="${MERGE_MODEL_DEVELOP:-}" ;;
    main) MERGE_MODE="${MERGE_MODEL_MAIN:-}" ;;
  esac
  if [ -z "${MERGE_MODE}" ] && [ -n "${MERGE_MODEL:-}" ]; then
    print_warn "MERGE_MODEL is the legacy single key — read for '${DESTINATION_BRANCH}'; the reshape writes MERGE_MODEL_DEVELOP and MERGE_MODEL_MAIN."
    MERGE_MODE="${MERGE_MODEL}"
  fi
  [ "${MERGE_MODE}" = "pr" ] || MERGE_MODE="direct"

  if [ "${SOURCE_BRANCH}" = "main" ]; then
    print_error "ERROR: merges FROM 'main' are not allowed."
    print_warn "- 'main' is the release branch; nothing is authored there"
    print_warn "- name a feature branch, or 'develop', as the source"
    exit 1
  fi

  if [ "${DESTINATION_BRANCH}" = "main" ] && [ "${CURRENT_BRANCH}" != "develop" ]; then
    print_error "ERROR: merges INTO 'main' are only allowed from 'develop'."
    print_warn "- you are on '${CURRENT_BRANCH}'"
    print_warn "- run \`mise run code:merge:develop\` first, then merge develop into main"
    exit 1
  fi

  if [ "${SOURCE_BRANCH}" = "${DESTINATION_BRANCH}" ]; then
    print_error "ERROR: '${SOURCE_BRANCH}' cannot be merged into itself."
    exit 1
  fi

  if [ "${CURRENT_BRANCH}" = "${DESTINATION_BRANCH}" ]; then
    print_error "ERROR: you are already on '${DESTINATION_BRANCH}'."
    print_warn "- run this from the branch being merged, so it is the one that is checked"
    exit 1
  fi

  # Asked up front, not discovered at the checkout after the whole-tree hook pass.
  if ! git show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/heads/${DESTINATION_BRANCH}"; then
    print_error "ERROR: branch '${DESTINATION_BRANCH}' does not exist locally."
    print_warn "- this repo's branch model needs both 'develop' and 'main': work is"
    print_warn "  authored on feature branches, integrated on 'develop', and reaches"
    print_warn "  'main' only by merge"
    print_warn "- create it (\`git branch ${DESTINATION_BRANCH}\`, or fetch it from the"
    print_warn "  remote) and run this again"
    exit 1
  fi

  # A branch checked out in a linked worktree cannot be checked out in another, so the checkout happens in the main one.
  local IS_WORKTREE=false
  local MAIN_WORKTREE_PATH=""
  local MAIN_WORKTREE_BRANCH=""
  local RESTORE_BRANCH=""
  local ORIGINAL_DIR="${PWD}"

  if is_git_worktree; then
    IS_WORKTREE=true
    MAIN_WORKTREE_PATH=$(get_main_worktree_path)
    MAIN_WORKTREE_BRANCH=$(git -C "${MAIN_WORKTREE_PATH}" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
    if [ "${MAIN_WORKTREE_BRANCH}" != "${DESTINATION_BRANCH}" ]; then
      RESTORE_BRANCH="${MAIN_WORKTREE_BRANCH}"
    fi
  else
    RESTORE_BRANCH="${CURRENT_BRANCH}"
  fi

  print_wait "Checking if any untracked files exist ... "
  if has_untracked_files; then
    print_error "ERROR"
    print_error "- Untracked files exist, please commit or remove them and try again."
    exit 1
  fi
  print_ok

  print_wait "Checking if any uncommitted changes exist ... "
  if has_uncommitted_changes; then
    print_error "ERROR"
    print_error "- Uncommitted changes exist, please commit or remove them and try again."
    exit 1
  fi
  print_ok

  # Only under `direct`: `pr` publishes the source branch as its first act.
  if [ "${MERGE_MODE}" = "direct" ]; then
    print_wait "Checking if any unpushed commits exist on ${SOURCE_BRANCH} ... "
    if is_local_branch "${SOURCE_BRANCH}"; then
      print_yellow "local branch"
    elif has_unpushed_commits "${SOURCE_BRANCH}"; then
      print_error "ERROR"
      print_error "- Unpushed commits exist on '${SOURCE_BRANCH}', please push them and try again."
      exit 1
    else
      print_ok
    fi
  fi

  precommit_safety_net

  # Everything below is the local merge, which only `direct` performs.
  if [ "${MERGE_MODE}" = "pr" ]; then
    open_pull_request "${DESTINATION_BRANCH}" "${SOURCE_BRANCH}"
    return 0
  fi

  if [ "${IS_WORKTREE}" = true ]; then
    print_wait "Switching to main worktree at ${MAIN_WORKTREE_PATH} ... "
    if ! cd "${MAIN_WORKTREE_PATH}"; then
      print_error "ERROR"
      print_error "FAILED to switch to main worktree at '${MAIN_WORKTREE_PATH}'!"
      exit 1
    fi
    print_ok
  fi

  print_wait "Checkout ${DESTINATION_BRANCH} branch ... "
  if ! git checkout "${DESTINATION_BRANCH}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    print_error "ERROR"
    print_error "FAILED to checkout '${DESTINATION_BRANCH}' branch!"
    exit 1
  fi
  print_ok

  # Tags too: a stale tag list is how a version gets reused.
  print_wait "Pulling latest changes from ${DESTINATION_BRANCH} branch ... "
  if ! git pull origin "${DESTINATION_BRANCH}" --tags >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    [ -n "${RESTORE_BRANCH}" ] && git checkout "${RESTORE_BRANCH}" -q >/dev/null 2>&1
    print_error "ERROR"
    print_error "FAILED to pull latest changes from '${DESTINATION_BRANCH}' branch!"
    exit 1
  fi
  print_ok

  # A conflict leaves the tree mid-merge on purpose: aborting would discard which files disagree.
  print_wait "Merging ${SOURCE_BRANCH} into ${DESTINATION_BRANCH} ... "
  if ! git merge --no-ff --no-edit "${SOURCE_BRANCH}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    print_error "ERROR"
    print_error "FAILED to merge ${SOURCE_BRANCH} into ${DESTINATION_BRANCH}!"
    print_warn "- the tree is left mid-merge; resolve the conflicts and commit,"
    print_warn "  or run \`git merge --abort\` to undo it"
    exit 1
  fi
  print_ok

  print_wait "Pushing ${DESTINATION_BRANCH} branch to origin ... "
  if ! git push origin "${DESTINATION_BRANCH}" --follow-tags >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    print_error "ERROR"
    print_error "FAILED to push ${DESTINATION_BRANCH} branch to origin!"
    exit 1
  fi
  print_ok

  if [ -n "${RESTORE_BRANCH}" ]; then
    if [ "${IS_WORKTREE}" = true ]; then
      print_wait "Restoring main worktree to ${RESTORE_BRANCH} branch ... "
    else
      print_wait "Checkout back to ${RESTORE_BRANCH} branch ... "
    fi
    if ! git checkout "${RESTORE_BRANCH}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      print_error "ERROR"
      print_error "FAILED to checkout back to '${RESTORE_BRANCH}' branch!"
      exit 1
    fi
    print_ok
  fi

  cd "${ORIGINAL_DIR}" || true

  print_newline
  print_success "Merge completed successfully!"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash

#MISE description="Renders the prompt for tasks no stack has filled yet"
#MISE hide=true

# Pulls in its own printers; the guard in `helpers` makes a second source a no-op.
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}/.config/mise/tasks/_scripts/helpers"

readonly PLACEHOLDER_MARKER="#PLACEHOLDER"

# List every task file in this repo still carrying the marker, as task names.
# `_scripts/` is excluded: this file names the marker itself.
placeholder_tasks() {
  local root="${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}/.config/mise/tasks"
  [ -d "$root" ] || return 0
  # `|| true`: no match is an empty list, not a `pipefail` error.
  { grep -rl --exclude-dir=_scripts -- "${PLACEHOLDER_MARKER}" "$root" 2>/dev/null || true; } |
    command sed -e "s#^${root}/##" -e 's#/#:#g' |
    command sort
}

# placeholder_notice <task-name> <one-line reason>
placeholder_notice() {
  local task="$1" reason="$2"
  local pending
  pending="$(placeholder_tasks | command tr '\n' ' ')"

  print_warn "${task} is not configured yet — ${reason}"
  print_newline

  if [ -n "${pending// /}" ]; then
    print_yellow "Unconfigured in this repo: ${pending% }"
    print_newline
  fi

  print_yellow "To configure them:"
  print_yellow "  /vwf:architecture   pin this repo's stack axes (do this first)"
  print_yellow "  /stackgen           materialize the packs that fill them"
  print_newline

  return 0
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash

#MISE description="Format, lint and security-scan all code"
#MISE dir="{{ config_root }}"

#USAGE flag "--debug" help="emit debug logs"
#USAGE flag "--fix" help="apply fixes"

set -euo pipefail
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}/.config/mise/tasks/_scripts/helpers"

# `${ARR[@]+"${ARR[@]}"}`: under `set -u` an empty array is unbound on older bash.
FLAGS=()
[[ "${usage_debug:-false}" == "true" ]] && FLAGS+=("--debug")
[[ "${usage_fix:-false}" == "true" ]] && FLAGS+=("--fix")

SEC_FLAGS=()
[[ "${usage_debug:-false}" == "true" ]] && SEC_FLAGS+=("--debug")

# Compiled stacks (a typed monorepo, say) prepend a typecheck here:
#   print_subheader "Typechecking ..."; mise run code:check

print_subheader "Formatting ..."
mise run code:format ${FLAGS[@]+"${FLAGS[@]}"}

print_subheader "Linting ..."
mise run code:lint ${FLAGS[@]+"${FLAGS[@]}"}

print_subheader "Security scanning ..."
mise run code:sec ${SEC_FLAGS[@]+"${SEC_FLAGS[@]}"}

#!/usr/bin/env bash

#MISE description="Count lines of code"
#MISE dir="{{ config_root }}"

set -euo pipefail
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}/.config/mise/tasks/_scripts/helpers"

print_header "Counting lines of code ..."

counts=""
# `|| true`: git grep exits 1 on no match, a status `set -e` would take.
counts=$(git -C "${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}" grep -I -c '' -- . 2>/dev/null) || true

if [ -z "${counts}" ]; then
  print_warn "No tracked text files."
  exit 0
fi

# Grouped by extension, top ten; split on the LAST colon so a path holding one still parses.
print_subheader "By extension"
printf '%s\n' "${counts}" | awk '
  {
    at = match($0, /:[0-9]+$/)
    if (at == 0) next
    n = substr($0, at + 1) + 0
    path = substr($0, 1, at - 1)

    slash = split(path, parts, "/")
    base = parts[slash]
    dot = split(base, pieces, ".")
    ext = (dot > 1) ? "." pieces[dot] : "(none)"

    lines[ext] += n
    files[ext] += 1
  }
  END {
    for (e in lines) printf "%12d  %6d  %s\n", lines[e], files[e], e
  }
' | sort -rn | head -10

printf '%s\n' "${counts}" | awk '
  {
    at = match($0, /:[0-9]+$/)
    if (at == 0) next
    total += substr($0, at + 1) + 0
    count += 1
  }
  END { printf "\n%12d lines in %d tracked text files\n", total, count }
'

#!/usr/bin/env bash

#MISE description="Format the repo's files"
#MISE dir="{{ config_root }}"

#USAGE flag "--debug" help="emit debug logs"
#USAGE flag "--fix" help="apply fixes"
#USAGE arg "[files]" var=#true help="files to format (default: the whole repo)"

set -euo pipefail
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}/.config/mise/tasks/_scripts/helpers"

# The `format` hook calls this task: an overlay keeps the file argument and the shfmt default.

files=()
eval "files+=(${usage_files:-})"

CONFIG="${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}/.config/dprint.json"

# dprint finds no config under `.config/`, so every call names it.
[[ "${usage_debug:-false}" == "true" ]] && LOG_LEVEL="debug" || LOG_LEVEL="warn"
[[ "${usage_fix:-false}" == "true" ]] && ACTION="fmt" || ACTION="check"

# `./`-prefixed and after `--`, so a leading `-` is never an option; dprint reads each path as a glob.
dprint_files=()
for f in ${files[@]+"${files[@]}"}; do
  case "${f}" in
    /* | ./*) dprint_files+=("${f}") ;;
    *) dprint_files+=("./${f}") ;;
  esac
done

if [ -f "${CONFIG}" ]; then
  dprint "${ACTION}" \
    --config "${CONFIG}" \
    --allow-no-files \
    --log-level "${LOG_LEVEL}" \
    -- ${dprint_files[@]+"${dprint_files[@]}"}
else
  print_warn "No .config/dprint.json — skipping the whitespace pass."
  print_yellow "The formatter component owns that file; materialize it first."
fi

# The flags match the shell gate's, so formatting and checking cannot disagree.
if command -v shfmt >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  shell_scope=()
  while IFS= read -r shell_file; do
    if [ -n "${shell_file}" ]; then
      shell_scope+=("${shell_file}")
    fi
  done < <(shell_files_in_scope ${files[@]+"${files[@]}"})

  if [ "${#shell_scope[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
    if [ "${ACTION}" = "fmt" ]; then
      shfmt -w -i 2 -ci "${shell_scope[@]}"
    else
      shfmt -d -i 2 -ci "${shell_scope[@]}"
    fi
  fi
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash

#MISE description="Validate the local git-config carries the forge identity and signing setup"

#USAGE flag "--fix" help="Write the identity from the forge variables and set the signing keys in the local git-config"

set -euo pipefail
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}/.config/mise/tasks/_scripts/helpers"

print_wait "Validating git-config ... "

FIXIT="${usage_fix:-false}"

# Identity and signing: PER-REPO, required, equal to GITHUB_/GITLAB_/GIT_USER_NAME & kin
ORIGIN=$(git remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null || true)
# Userinfo is stripped from the authority alone, so an `@` in the path cannot spoof the host.
case "$ORIGIN" in
  *://*)
    HOST=${ORIGIN#*://}
    HOST=${HOST%%/*}
    ;;
  *)
    HOST=${ORIGIN%%/*}
    case "$HOST" in
      *:*) HOST=${HOST%%:*} ;;
      *) HOST="" ;;
    esac
    ;;
esac
HOST=${HOST##*@}
HOST=${HOST%%:*}
case "$HOST" in
  github.com | *.github.com) FORGE="GITHUB" ;;
  gitlab.com | *.gitlab.com) FORGE="GITLAB" ;;
  *) FORGE="GIT" ;;
esac

VAR_NAME="${FORGE}_USER_NAME"
VAR_EMAIL="${FORGE}_EMAIL"
VAR_KEY="${FORGE}_SIGNING_KEY"

local_get() { git config --local --get -- "$1" 2>/dev/null || true; }

# Prints every key that misses its required value and returns 1 when there is one.
check() {
  local failures="" unset_vars="" spec key var expected actual
  for spec in "user.name=${VAR_NAME}" "user.email=${VAR_EMAIL}" "user.signingkey=${VAR_KEY}"; do
    key=${spec%%=*}
    var=${spec#*=}
    expected="${!var:-}"
    actual=$(local_get "$key")
    if [ -z "$expected" ]; then
      unset_vars+="${var}"$'\n'
      failures+="- ${key}: expected \$${var} (unset), actual ${actual:-<unset>}"$'\n'
    elif [ "$actual" != "$expected" ]; then
      failures+="- ${key}: expected '${expected}' (\$${var}), actual ${actual:-<unset>}"$'\n'
    fi
  done
  for spec in commit.gpgsign=true tag.gpgsign=true gpg.format=ssh; do
    key=${spec%%=*}
    expected=${spec#*=}
    actual=$(local_get "$key")
    if [ "$actual" != "$expected" ]; then
      failures+="- ${key}: expected '${expected}', actual ${actual:-<unset>}"$'\n'
    fi
  done
  for key in gpg.program gpg.ssh.program; do
    actual=$(local_get "$key")
    if [ -n "$actual" ]; then
      failures+="- ${key}: expected unset, actual '${actual}'"$'\n'
    fi
  done

  if [ -z "$failures" ]; then
    print_ok
    return 0
  fi
  print_error "ERROR"
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
    print_warn "$line"
  done <<<"$failures"
  if [ -n "$unset_vars" ]; then
    print_yellow "Export the variables the identity is read from (origin host resolves to ${FORGE}):"
    while IFS= read -r var; do
      [ -n "$var" ] || continue
      print_yellow "  export ${var}=..."
    done <<<"$unset_vars"
  fi
  print_error "Please run \`mise run ${MISE_TASK_NAME:-code:git-config} --fix\` to set them"
  return 1
}

if [ "$FIXIT" = "true" ]; then
  missing=""
  for var in "$VAR_NAME" "$VAR_EMAIL" "$VAR_KEY"; do
    [ -n "${!var:-}" ] || missing+=" ${var}"
  done
  if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
    print_error "ERROR"
    print_error "Cannot fix — unset:${missing}. Export them and re-run; nothing was written."
    exit 1
  fi
  print_newline
  # git resolved the identity before this hook ran, so a run that changed a key fails on purpose.
  CHANGED=false
  for spec in "user.name=${!VAR_NAME}" "user.email=${!VAR_EMAIL}" "user.signingkey=${!VAR_KEY}" commit.gpgsign=true tag.gpgsign=true gpg.format=ssh; do
    key=${spec%%=*}
    if [ "$(local_get "$key")" != "${spec#*=}" ]; then
      print_wait "- setting ${key} ... "
      git config --local -- "$key" "${spec#*=}"
      CHANGED=true
      print_ok
    fi
  done
  for key in gpg.program gpg.ssh.program; do
    if [ -n "$(local_get "$key")" ]; then
      print_wait "- unsetting ${key} ... "
      git config --local --unset-all -- "$key"
      CHANGED=true
      print_ok
    fi
  done
  print_wait "Re-validating git-config ... "
  check
  if [ "$CHANGED" = "true" ]; then
    print_warn "identity corrected — re-run the commit"
    exit 1
  fi
  exit 0
fi

check

#!/usr/bin/env bash

#MISE description="Refresh the graphify knowledge graph, run by the graphify-refresh post-commit hook (code only, no LLM)"
#MISE dir="{{ config_root }}"

#USAGE flag "--force" help="Rebuild even when the last commit only touched graphify-out/"

set -euo pipefail
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}/.config/mise/tasks/_scripts/helpers"

# Run by pre-commit's graphify-refresh post-commit hook; graphify's own git hook is removed.

if [ "${GRAPHIFY_SKIP_HOOK:-0}" = "1" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

if ! command -v graphify >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  print_warn "graphify is not on PATH — graph not refreshed (MISE_ENV=dev mise run setup:all)"
  exit 0
fi

# Only the main checkout holds a graph; a linked worktree never rebuilds one.
GIT_DIR_ABS="$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)" && pwd -P)"
GIT_COMMON_ABS="$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" && pwd -P)"
if [ "${GIT_DIR_ABS}" != "${GIT_COMMON_ABS}" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

# Never mid-rebase, merge or cherry-pick: the rebuild would race the working tree.
for marker in rebase-merge rebase-apply; do
  [ -d "${GIT_DIR_ABS}/${marker}" ] && exit 0
done
for marker in MERGE_HEAD CHERRY_PICK_HEAD; do
  [ -f "${GIT_DIR_ABS}/${marker}" ] && exit 0
done

force=()
if [[ "${usage_force:-false}" == "true" ]]; then
  force=(--force)
else
  # A first commit has no parent, so every file it tracks counts as changed.
  if git rev-parse -q --verify HEAD~1 >/dev/null; then
    changed="$(git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD)"
  else
    changed="$(git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
  fi
  # A commit touching only graphify-out/ is the previous rebuild landing; rebuilding would loop.
  if [ -z "$(printf '%s\n' "${changed}" | grep -v '^graphify-out/' || true)" ]; then
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# Pinned so louvain's set iteration, and so the community ids, stay stable across runs.
export PYTHONHASHSEED=0

LOG="${HOME}/.cache/graphify-rebuild.log"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "${LOG}")"

# One rebuild at a time: mkdir is atomic, and the lock holds its owner's PID.
LOCK="${GIT_DIR_ABS}/graphify-refresh.lock"
TAKEOVER="${LOCK}.takeover"

# A skip, or a lost race, is never a failure of the commit.
skip() {
  print_yellow "graphify: $1 — skipped (lock: ${LOCK})"
  exit 0
}

# Held: a live PID, or no PID yet on a lock under ten minutes old.
lock_is_held() {
  local holder
  holder="$(cat "${LOCK}/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ -n "${holder}" ]; then
    kill -0 "${holder}" 2>/dev/null
  else
    [ -d "${LOCK}" ] && [ -z "$(find "${LOCK}" -maxdepth 0 -mmin +10 2>/dev/null)" ]
  fi
}

if ! mkdir "${LOCK}" 2>/dev/null; then
  if lock_is_held; then
    skip "a refresh is already running"
  fi
  # A takeover dir left by a killed run is stale after ten minutes; only the
  # run whose mv succeeds clears it, and only if what it moved is still old.
  if [ -n "$(find "${TAKEOVER}" -maxdepth 0 -mmin +10 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
    dead="${TAKEOVER}.dead.$$"
    if mv "${TAKEOVER}" "${dead}" 2>/dev/null; then
      if [ -z "$(find "${dead}" -maxdepth 0 -mmin +10 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
        # It moved a live takeover: put an equivalent one back and step aside.
        mkdir "${TAKEOVER}" 2>/dev/null || true
        rm -rf "${dead}" || true
        skip "another run is taking over the lock"
      fi
      rm -rf "${dead}" || true
    fi
  fi
  # Only the run that makes the takeover dir may replace a stale lock.
  if ! mkdir "${TAKEOVER}" 2>/dev/null; then
    skip "another run is taking over the lock"
  fi
  # Re-checked under the takeover: the lock may have changed since.
  if ! mkdir "${LOCK}" 2>/dev/null; then
    if lock_is_held; then
      rmdir "${TAKEOVER}" 2>/dev/null || true
      skip "a refresh is already running"
    fi
    rm -rf "${LOCK}" || true
    # A plain run may win the freed lock first; the rebuild is then its.
    if ! mkdir "${LOCK}" 2>/dev/null; then
      rmdir "${TAKEOVER}" 2>/dev/null || true
      skip "another run took the lock first"
    fi
  fi
  rmdir "${TAKEOVER}" 2>/dev/null || true
fi
# This task holds the lock until the rebuild writes its own PID over it.
echo "$$" >"${LOCK}/pid" 2>/dev/null || true

print_yellow "graphify: refreshing the graph in the background (log: ${LOG})"
# Detached so the commit returns at once; the rebuild removes the lock only while it is its own.
# shellcheck disable=SC2016
nohup bash -c 'lock="$1"
shift
release() { [ "$(cat "${lock}/pid" 2>/dev/null)" = "$$" ] && rm -rf "${lock}"; }
trap release EXIT
echo "$$" >"${lock}/pid"
graphify update . "$@"' graphify-refresh "${LOCK}" ${force[@]+"${force[@]}"} >>"${LOG}" 2>&1 </dev/null &
echo "$!" >"${LOCK}/pid" 2>/dev/null || true
disown
exit 0

#MISE description="Security scan the repo"
#MISE dir="{{ config_root }}"

#USAGE flag "--debug" help="emit debug logs"

#USAGE arg "[files]" var=#true help="accepted for the gate's sake; both scanners read the tree"

# shellcheck source=/dev/null

# The `sec` hook calls this with `--staged`: the staged diff only, no dependency scan.

SECRETS_CONFIG="${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}/.config/gitleaks.toml"
VULN_CONFIG="${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}/.config/grype.yaml"

if [ "${usage_staged:-false}" = "true" ]; then
  if command -v gitleaks >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    print_wait "Scanning the staged changes for secrets ... "
    if [ -f "${SECRETS_CONFIG}" ]; then
      gitleaks git --staged --config "${SECRETS_CONFIG}" --redact=50
    else
      gitleaks git --staged --redact=50
    fi
    print_ok
  else
    print_warn "gitleaks is not on PATH — skipping the staged secret scan."
  fi
  exit 0
fi

if command -v gitleaks >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  print_wait "Scanning for committed secrets ... "
  # The overlay skips a gitignored `.env` in `dir` mode only; never allowlist it in the repo config.
  OVERLAY=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gitleaks-overlay.XXXXXX")
  trap 'rm -f "${OVERLAY}"' EXIT
  {
    echo '[extend]'
    if [ -f "${SECRETS_CONFIG}" ]; then
      echo "path = \"${SECRETS_CONFIG}\""
    else
      echo 'useDefault = true'
    fi
    cat <<'EOF'

[allowlist]
paths = ['(^|/)\.env$', '(^|/)\.env\..*']
EOF
  } >"${OVERLAY}"
  gitleaks dir . --config "${OVERLAY}" --redact=50
  print_ok
else
  print_warn "gitleaks is not on PATH — skipping the secret scan."
fi

if command -v grype >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  print_wait "Scanning dependencies for known vulnerabilities ... "
  grype_status=0
  if [ -f "${VULN_CONFIG}" ]; then
    grype "dir:${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}" --config "${VULN_CONFIG}" --fail-on medium || grype_status=$?
  else
    grype "dir:${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}" --fail-on medium || grype_status=$?
  fi
  if [ "$grype_status" -ne 0 ]; then
    print_error "ERROR"
    if [ -f "${VULN_CONFIG}" ]; then
      print_warn "To accept a finding, add its vulnerability id under ignore: in .config/grype.yaml with a one-line reason — see the grype conventions."
    else
      print_warn "No .config/grype.yaml to accept a finding in — materialize the grype component first, then add the id under ignore: with a one-line reason."
    fi
    exit "$grype_status"
  fi
  print_ok
else
  print_warn "grype is not on PATH — skipping the vulnerability scan."
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash

#MISE description="List git worktrees across this repo and every member"

set -euo pipefail
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}/.config/mise/tasks/_scripts/helpers"

# Ahead/behind against origin/HEAD, falling back to the literal `main`.
default_branch() {
  local ref
  ref="$(git -C "$1" symbolic-ref -q refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ -n "$ref" ]; then
    echo "${ref##*/}"
  else
    echo "main"
  fi
}

report() {
  local repo="$1" label="$2"
  local base worktrees
  base="$(default_branch "$repo")"

  worktrees="$(git -C "$repo" worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null | awk '/^worktree /{print $2}')"
  [ -n "$worktrees" ] || return 0

  print_header "${label}  (base: ${base})"

  while read -r wt; do
    [ -n "$wt" ] || continue
    local branch counts ahead behind
    branch="$(git -C "$wt" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo '?')"

    if git -C "$wt" rev-parse --verify --quiet "origin/${base}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      counts="$(git -C "$wt" rev-list --left-right --count "origin/${base}...HEAD" 2>/dev/null || printf '0\t0')"
      behind="$(echo "$counts" | awk '{print $1}')"
      ahead="$(echo "$counts" | awk '{print $2}')"
      print_yellow "  ${branch}  +${ahead}/-${behind}  ${wt}"
    else
      print_yellow "  ${branch}  (no origin/${base})  ${wt}"
    fi
  done <<<"$worktrees"

  print_newline
}

report "${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}" "$(basename "${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}")"

# `members` answers for either linkage.

while read -r member; do
  [ -n "$member" ] || continue
  report "${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}/${member}" "${member}"
done < <(members)

#!/usr/bin/env bash

#MISE description="Check for the workflow plugin, then update every marketplace and plugin"
#MISE hide=true

set -euo pipefail
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}/.config/mise/tasks/_scripts/helpers"

if ! command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  print_warn "claude is not on PATH — skipping AI setup."
  print_yellow "Install it from https://claude.com/code, then re-run this task."
  exit 0
fi

# Project scope resolves against the working directory.
cd "${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}"
ROOT="$(pwd -P)"

# The rows that hold here, as `<id>|<scope>`: user scope, or project or local scope
# whose projectPath resolves to this repo — never another repo's.
plugins_here() {
  local rows id scope path
  rows="$(claude plugin list --json |
    jq -r '.[] | select(.scope == "user" or .scope == "project" or .scope == "local") | "\(.id)|\(.scope)|\(.projectPath // "")"')"
  while IFS="|" read -r id scope path; do
    [ -n "${id}" ] || continue
    if [ "${scope}" != "user" ]; then
      [ -n "${path}" ] || continue
      path="$(cd "${path}" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" || continue
      [ "${path}" = "${ROOT}" ] || continue
    fi
    echo "${id}|${scope}"
  done <<<"${rows}"
}

# Installed here at any of those scopes: any is enough.
plugin_installed() { # <name@marketplace>
  local here
  here="$(plugins_here | cut -d"|" -f1)"
  grep -Fqx "$1" <<<"${here}"
}

marketplace_registered() { # <name>
  claude plugin marketplace list --json |
    jq -e --arg name "$1" 'any(.[]; .name == $name)' >/dev/null
}

# A pack's plugin: nothing when installed at either scope, else installed at user scope.
ensure_plugin() { # <name@marketplace> <source>
  if plugin_installed "$1"; then
    print_yellow "- $1: installed"
    return
  fi
  if ! marketplace_registered "${1##*@}" && ! claude plugin marketplace add "$2" </dev/null >/dev/null; then
    print_warn "- $1: adding its marketplace from $2 failed — continuing"
    return
  fi
  if ! claude plugin install --scope user "$1" </dev/null >/dev/null; then
    print_warn "- $1: installing it at user scope failed — continuing"
    return
  fi
  print_yellow "- $1: installed at user scope"
}

# The workflow plugin first; each pack's plugins in its own block below this one.
print_subheader "Checking plugins ..."
# >>> mise
if plugin_installed "vwf@virajp-plugins"; then
  print_yellow "- vwf@virajp-plugins: installed"
elif command -v pnpx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  print_yellow "- vwf@virajp-plugins: absent — installing it at user scope"
  if ! pnpx @virajp.dev/claude-plugins@latest --all; then
    print_warn "- the installer failed — continuing; re-run: pnpx @virajp.dev/claude-plugins@latest --all"
  fi
else
  print_warn "- vwf@virajp-plugins: absent, and pnpx is not on PATH — run: pnpx @virajp.dev/claude-plugins@latest --all"
fi
# <<< mise

# Whether or not anything was installed: every marketplace, then every plugin at its own scope.
print_subheader "Updating marketplaces ..."
if ! claude plugin marketplace update >/dev/null; then
  print_warn "- a marketplace update failed — updating plugins from what is cached"
fi

print_subheader "Updating plugins ..."
rows="$(plugins_here)"
while IFS='|' read -r plugin scope; do
  [ -n "${plugin}" ] || continue
  print_wait "- ${plugin} (${scope}) ... "
  if claude plugin update --scope "${scope}" "${plugin}" </dev/null >/dev/null; then
    print_ok
  else
    print_warn "failed — continuing"
  fi
done <<<"${rows}"

print_subheader "Pruning plugins nothing references ..."
if ! claude plugin autoremove --scope project --yes >/dev/null; then
  print_warn "- pruning failed — continuing"
fi

print_success "AI tooling reconciled."

#!/usr/bin/env bash

#MISE description="Set up everything this repo needs on your machine"
#MISE depends=["init"]

#USAGE flag "--all" help="Also set up every member project"

# A MARKED POSITION — MEMBER_FLAGS: one flag per member repo, named by its slug, below this comment:
#   #USAGE flag "--<slug>" help="Set up the <slug> project"
#USAGE flag "--api" help="Set up the api project"
#USAGE flag "--web" help="Set up the web project"

set -euo pipefail
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}/.config/mise/tasks/_scripts/helpers"

# MISE_ENV decides which conf.d files load; guessing it is wrong.
if [ -z "${MISE_ENV:-}" ]; then
  print_error "MISE_ENV is unset. On a developer machine run: MISE_ENV=dev mise run setup:all"
  exit 1
fi

# Idempotent and non-destructive: it installs the pins and moves none.
print_header "Setting up the toolchain ..."
mise run setup:mise

print_header "Setting up secrets ..."
mise run setup:secrets

print_header "Starting external services ..."
mise run setup:external:start

print_header "Setting up dependencies ..."
mise run setup:deps:all

print_header "Setting up commit hooks ..."
mise run setup:precommit

print_header "Setting up AI tooling ..."
mise run setup:ai

# Members only on request — `--all`, or a member's own `--<slug>` — each running its OWN task library
# from inside it, so its own miserc.toml is read. The slug is the member folder's name, slugified as the
# flags above were written; usage exposes `--<slug>` as `usage_<slug>` with `-` read as `_`.
while read -r member; do
  [ -n "$member" ] || continue
  slug="$(basename "$member" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | sed -E 's/[^a-z0-9]+/-/g; s/^-+//; s/-+$//')"
  flag="usage_${slug//-/_}"
  [[ "${usage_all:-false}" == "true" || "${!flag:-false}" == "true" ]] || continue
  print_header "Setting up ${member} ..."
  (cd "${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}/${member}" && mise run setup:all </dev/null)
done < <(members)

print_header "Setup complete!"

#!/usr/bin/env bash

#MISE description="Install pre-commit hooks; refuses to replace a foreign hook manager"
#MISE hide=true

#USAGE flag "--force" help="Replace a foreign hook manager (core.hooksPath, husky, lefthook) with pre-commit"
#USAGE flag "--update" help="Run pre-commit autoupdate first, moving every hook rev to its latest tag"

set -euo pipefail
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}/.config/mise/tasks/_scripts/helpers"

CONFIG=".config/pre-commit-config.yaml"
FORCE="${usage_force:-false}"
UPDATE="${usage_update:-false}"

if [ ! -f "${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}/${CONFIG}" ]; then
  print_warn "No ${CONFIG} — skipping hook installation."
  print_yellow "The hook-runner component owns that file; materialize it first."
  exit 0
fi

# Strip graphify's marked block from a hook, deleting the file when nothing but a shebang and blank lines is left.
strip_graphify_block() {
  local file="$1" name="$2"
  if [ ! -f "$file" ] || ! grep -q "^# ${name}-start$" "$file"; then
    return 0
  fi
  awk -v s="# ${name}-start" -v e="# ${name}-end" '$0 == s { skip = 1; next } skip && $0 == e { skip = 0; next } !skip' "$file" >"${file}.tmp"
  if grep -qv -e '^#!' -e '^[[:space:]]*$' "${file}.tmp"; then
    # Written through the original file so its exec bit survives.
    cat "${file}.tmp" >"$file"
    rm -f "${file}.tmp"
  else
    rm -f "$file" "${file}.tmp"
  fi
}

# graphify's raw hooks pin a Python path; strip them before any refusal below, unless core.hooksPath is set, where they are only named.
HOOKS_PATH=$(git config --get core.hooksPath 2>/dev/null || true)
HOOKS_DIR="$(git rev-parse --git-path hooks)"
graphify_marked() {
  grep -qs "^# graphify-hook-start$" "${HOOKS_DIR}/$1" || grep -qs "^# graphify-checkout-hook-start$" "${HOOKS_DIR}/$2"
}
if [ -n "$HOOKS_PATH" ]; then
  # A core.hooksPath directory is another manager's, possibly outside the repo, so its hooks are never edited here.
  if graphify_marked post-commit post-checkout || graphify_marked post-commit.legacy post-checkout.legacy; then
    print_warn "graphify's raw hooks sit under core.hooksPath (${HOOKS_PATH}) — left alone. Remove them by hand:"
    print_yellow "  graphify hook uninstall   # or delete each '# graphify-*-start' … '-end' block under ${HOOKS_DIR}"
  fi
else
  if graphify_marked post-commit post-checkout; then
    print_subheader "Removing graphify's raw git hooks ..."
    if command -v graphify >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      graphify hook uninstall
    else
      strip_graphify_block "${HOOKS_DIR}/post-commit" graphify-hook
      strip_graphify_block "${HOOKS_DIR}/post-checkout" graphify-checkout-hook
    fi
  fi
  # An earlier plain install may already have chained one as <hook>.legacy; graphify's uninstall never looks there.
  if graphify_marked post-commit.legacy post-checkout.legacy; then
    print_subheader "Removing graphify's chained .legacy hooks ..."
    strip_graphify_block "${HOOKS_DIR}/post-commit.legacy" graphify-hook
    strip_graphify_block "${HOOKS_DIR}/post-checkout.legacy" graphify-checkout-hook
  fi
fi

# graphify's merge driver goes too: its attribute line and its local git-config section, never the attributes file.
ATTRIBUTES="${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}/.gitattributes"
if grep -qs 'merge=graphify' "$ATTRIBUTES"; then
  print_subheader "Removing graphify's merge attribute ..."
  grep -v 'merge=graphify' "$ATTRIBUTES" >"${ATTRIBUTES}.tmp" || true
  cat "${ATTRIBUTES}.tmp" >"$ATTRIBUTES"
  rm -f "${ATTRIBUTES}.tmp"
fi
if git config --local --get-regexp '^merge\.graphify\.' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  print_subheader "Removing graphify's merge driver from the local git config ..."
  git config --local --remove-section merge.graphify
fi

# A foreign hook manager is never touched without `--force`; the effective core.hooksPath is what is read.
FOREIGN=""
LOCAL_HOOKS_PATH=$(git config --local --get core.hooksPath 2>/dev/null || true)
GLOBAL_HOOKS_PATH=$(git config --global --get core.hooksPath 2>/dev/null || true)
SYSTEM_HOOKS_PATH=$(git config --system --get core.hooksPath 2>/dev/null || true)
HOOK_FILE="${HOOKS_DIR}/pre-commit"
TAKEN_OVER=false
if [ -z "$HOOKS_PATH" ] && [ -f "$HOOK_FILE" ] && grep -q "generated by pre-commit" "$HOOK_FILE"; then
  TAKEN_OVER=true
fi
# A value outside the repo wins: unsetting the local one would leave it in force.
GLOBAL_ONLY=false
if [ -n "$GLOBAL_HOOKS_PATH" ]; then
  GLOBAL_ONLY=true
  FOREIGN+="- core.hooksPath is set to '${GLOBAL_HOOKS_PATH}' by the global git-config"$'\n'
fi
if [ -n "$SYSTEM_HOOKS_PATH" ]; then
  GLOBAL_ONLY=true
  FOREIGN+="- core.hooksPath is set to '${SYSTEM_HOOKS_PATH}' by the system git-config"$'\n'
fi
if [ -n "$LOCAL_HOOKS_PATH" ]; then
  FOREIGN+="- core.hooksPath is set to '${LOCAL_HOOKS_PATH}' in the local git-config"$'\n'
elif [ -n "$HOOKS_PATH" ] && [ "$GLOBAL_ONLY" != "true" ]; then
  GLOBAL_ONLY=true
  FOREIGN+="- core.hooksPath is set to '${HOOKS_PATH}' outside the local git-config"$'\n'
fi
if [ "$TAKEN_OVER" != "true" ]; then
  for path in .husky lefthook.yml lefthook.yaml lefthook.toml lefthook.json .lefthook.yml .lefthook.yaml .lefthook.toml .lefthook.json; do
    if [ -e "${MISE_PROJECT_ROOT}/${path}" ]; then
      FOREIGN+="- ${path} is present"$'\n'
    fi
  done
fi

if [ -n "$FOREIGN" ]; then
  if [ "$FORCE" = "true" ] && [ "$GLOBAL_ONLY" != "true" ]; then
    print_warn "Replacing the existing hook setup (--force):"
  else
    print_error "Another hook manager owns this repo's hooks — refusing to replace it:"
  fi
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
    print_yellow "$line"
  done <<<"$FOREIGN"
  if [ "$GLOBAL_ONLY" = "true" ]; then
    print_yellow "That value is outside this repo, and --force never edits it. Unset it by hand:"
    if [ -n "$GLOBAL_HOOKS_PATH" ]; then
      print_yellow "  git config --global --unset-all core.hooksPath"
    fi
    if [ -n "$SYSTEM_HOOKS_PATH" ]; then
      print_yellow "  git config --system --unset-all core.hooksPath"
    fi
    if [ -z "$GLOBAL_HOOKS_PATH" ] && [ -z "$SYSTEM_HOOKS_PATH" ]; then
      print_yellow "  git config --show-origin --get core.hooksPath   # to find which file sets it"
    fi
    print_yellow "then re-run this task."
    exit 1
  fi
  if [ "$FORCE" != "true" ]; then
    print_yellow "To hand the hooks to pre-commit, run these by hand:"
    print_yellow "  git config --local --unset-all core.hooksPath"
    print_yellow "  pre-commit install --config ${CONFIG} --install-hooks --overwrite"
    print_yellow "or re-run this task with --force, which does the same. Then, so this stops firing:"
    print_yellow "  delete .husky/ or the lefthook file, and drop a package.json \"prepare\" script that runs husky"
    print_yellow "  (it sets core.hooksPath again on every install) — this task deletes nothing."
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# `autoupdate` rewrites every `rev:`, so only under `--update`.
if [ "$UPDATE" = "true" ]; then
  print_subheader "Updating pre-commit hooks ..."
  pre-commit autoupdate --config "${CONFIG}"
fi

# The hook types come from `default_install_hook_types`; without `--overwrite` a hand-written hook is chained as `.legacy`.
print_subheader "Installing pre-commit hooks ..."
if [ "$FORCE" = "true" ]; then
  git config --local --unset-all core.hooksPath || true
  pre-commit install --config "${CONFIG}" --install-hooks --overwrite
else
  pre-commit install --config "${CONFIG}" --install-hooks
fi
